p2_disposition.problem_confirmed: entity_host::scan_step ran the floating check_scan_facts after the integer classify_scan_words and before fp_state. A valid subnormal coordinate word (accepted by the raw classifier) reached its abs/range comparisons, which set the SSE denormal status (or would trap if unmasked) BEFORE the caller's state was captured, so the later after == state guard compared an already-modified state with itself.
guard_semantics_inspected: fp_state() only reads the registers (x87 control word, MXCSR) and the masks derived from them; it is the entry snapshot of the guard.

ScopedRounding::set saves the complete floating-point environment (including the sticky status bits) and its Drop restores it; the kernel is entered only inside that scope. Whatever the original C arithmetic does to the sticky bits inside it is therefore restored to the entry value, which is why the kernel's own use of subnormal operands needed no change.

Moving a read-only snapshot alone would not have been proof: the typed floating work (the abs/range comparisons) was the thing that changed the state. The fix therefore removes that work from production rather than reordering it.
The remaining float work before the guard is none: f32::from_bits is a move of the word's bits, and it now also follows the capture and the unsupported-environment refusal.
p2_disposition.change: classify_scan_words is the SOLE production validator of an entity-scan question (integer operations only; the same domains, order and messages). scan_step calls it, then captures fp_state and applies the existing unsupported-environment refusal (every exception masked in both units), and only then converts the words to floats for the kernel. check_scan_facts (the floating predicate) is #[cfg(test)] and exists only as the oracle of the differential test, whose corpus now includes the smallest and largest subnormal words of both signs. Error priority (malformed question first, then the environment refusal) is unchanged.
